loading_method.segment: Direct SQL INSERT or COPY INTO target tables
loading_method.rudderstack: File-download loading: download gzipped CSV from object storage, create staging table (CREATE TEMPORARY TABLE ... LIKE target), stream rows via pq.CopyIn, dedup via ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY id ORDER BY received_at DESC), INSERT into target table
loading_method.parity_impact: Different loading mechanism but functionally equivalent end state. RudderStack adds intermediate staging step for atomicity and dedup.

connection_pooling.segment: Standard connection pooling via Segment infrastructure; connection details configured via UI
connection_pooling.rudderstack: Per-upload connection via database/sql with sqlmiddleware wrapper; configurable connect_timeout, slow query threshold monitoring, transaction rollback timeout
connection_pooling.parity_impact: No impact on data output. Operational difference in connection lifecycle management.

ssh_tunneling.segment: Not supported natively for PostgreSQL warehouse connections
ssh_tunneling.rudderstack: SSH tunneling supported via tunnelling.Connect when SSH configuration is provided in destination config (host, port, user, private key). Connection routed through SSH tunnel transparently.
ssh_tunneling.parity_impact: RudderStack-unique connectivity feature. No impact on data schema or payload format.

ssl_support.segment: SSL supported via standard PostgreSQL connection parameters
ssl_support.rudderstack: SSL supported with sslmode parameter (disable, require, verify-ca). verify-ca mode supports server-ca.pem, client-cert.pem, client-key.pem certificate chain.
ssl_support.parity_impact: Equivalent SSL support. No impact on data schema or payload format.

schema_namespace.segment: Uses <source_slug> as the PostgreSQL schema name
schema_namespace.rudderstack: Uses configurable namespace (typically derived from source name) as the PostgreSQL schema name. Schema created via CREATE SCHEMA IF NOT EXISTS with SET search_path.
schema_namespace.parity_impact: Schema naming may differ. Functionally equivalent with different default naming convention.

data_types.segment: Uses VARCHAR(512) for strings, TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE for timestamps, FLOAT for numbers, BIGINT for integers, BOOLEAN for booleans
data_types.rudderstack: Uses text for strings (int→bigint, float→numeric, string→text, datetime→timestamptz, boolean→boolean, json→jsonb). All string columns use text type instead of VARCHAR(512).
data_types.parity_impact: Column type difference: Segment uses VARCHAR(512), RudderStack uses text. numeric vs FLOAT for decimal numbers. Both support the same value ranges in practice.

column_naming.segment: Flattened context fields use underscore notation: context_library_name, context_ip, etc.
column_naming.rudderstack: Same flattened underscore notation: context_library_name, context_ip, etc. Additional RudderStack-specific columns: uuid_ts, context_passed_ip, context_request_ip, context_traits_* for identify events.
column_naming.parity_impact: Column names are compatible. RudderStack includes additional metadata columns not present in Segment output.

additional_rudderstack_columns.description: RudderStack adds columns not present in Segment warehouse output

columns.uuid_ts: Timestamp when event was assigned a UUID by RudderStack Gateway
columns.context_passed_ip: IP address passed explicitly in event context
columns.context_request_ip: IP address from the HTTP request to Gateway
columns.context_traits_*: Duplicate of trait columns prefixed with context_traits_ in identifies table

additional_rudderstack_columns.parity_impact: Additional columns do not affect existing column values. They provide extra metadata useful for debugging and audit.

dedup_strategy.segment: INSERT with ON CONFLICT handling or COPY with post-load dedup
dedup_strategy.rudderstack: Staging table with ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY id ORDER BY received_at DESC) to keep only the latest version of each event. For users table, CASE-based newest-value aggregation computes latest trait per user across all identify events.
dedup_strategy.parity_impact: Different dedup mechanism but same end result: each event appears once, users table reflects latest trait values.

users_table_computation.segment: Upserts latest trait values into users table as identify events arrive
users_table_computation.rudderstack: LoadUserTables builds union staging table combining new identifies and existing users data, then computes latest trait values per user via CASE WHEN received_at > existing.received_at THEN new_value ELSE existing_value END aggregation. Configurable via skipComputingUserLatestTraits.
users_table_computation.parity_impact: Same end state (users table has latest traits). RudderStack uses batch recomputation vs Segment's incremental upsert.

merge_behavior.segment: Direct INSERT or upsert with no separate merge toggle
merge_behavior.rudderstack: Merge behavior controlled by Warehouse.postgres.allowMerge config (default: true). When merge is enabled, deletes matching rows from target table before inserting from staging table. When disabled, performs append-only INSERT. Special handling for discards table with multi-column join filter.
merge_behavior.parity_impact: When allowMerge is true (default), behavior matches Segment upsert semantics. When disabled, RudderStack switches to append-only which differs from Segment.

primary_keys.segment: Standard primary key on id column for event tables
primary_keys.rudderstack: Primary keys: users→id, identifies→id, discards→row_id. Partition keys: users→id, identifies→id, discards→(row_id, column_name, table_name). Used for dedup ROW_NUMBER() partitioning.
primary_keys.parity_impact: Compatible primary key strategy. RudderStack partition keys drive dedup granularity.

table_name_limit.segment: Standard PostgreSQL identifier length limit (63 characters default)
table_name_limit.rudderstack: Table name limit set to 127 characters. Staging table names generated via warehouseutils.StagingTableName with provider and table name prefix.
table_name_limit.parity_impact: RudderStack allows longer table names. No impact on standard event table names.

error_handling.segment: Standard error reporting via Segment UI
error_handling.rudderstack: Structured error mappings: ResourceNotFoundError (DNS failure, DB not exist, relation not exist, DB starting/shutting down), PermissionError (connection refused, auth failed, permission denied), ColumnCountError (1600 column limit). Errors mapped to job status codes for retry/abort decisions.
error_handling.parity_impact: No impact on data output. Operational difference in error classification and retry strategy.

context_library.parity_impact: Different SDK library identifiers in context.library fields. This is expected as each platform uses its own SDK.

critical_gaps.description: Segment uses VARCHAR(512) for string columns; RudderStack uses text. Segment uses FLOAT; RudderStack uses numeric. Both are functionally equivalent for typical payloads.
critical_gaps.remediation: No action required unless strict DDL parity is mandated. text and VARCHAR(512) store identical values.

critical_gaps.description: RudderStack adds uuid_ts, context_passed_ip, context_request_ip, and context_traits_* columns not present in Segment output.
critical_gaps.remediation: Additional columns are additive and do not affect shared column data. No action required for data parity.

critical_gaps.description: Different loading mechanism (Segment: direct INSERT/COPY; RudderStack: file-download with staging table and pq.CopyIn). End state is equivalent.
critical_gaps.remediation: No action required. Loading method is an implementation detail that does not affect data parity.

critical_gaps.description: Different SDK library names in context_library_name column (analytics.js vs rudder-sdk-js). This is expected behavior.
critical_gaps.remediation: No action required. SDK-level difference inherent to each platform.

critical_gaps.description: RudderStack supports SSH tunneling for PostgreSQL connections; Segment does not. This is a RudderStack-unique connectivity feature.
critical_gaps.remediation: No action required. Connectivity feature does not affect data schema or payload format.

required_settings.namespace: Schema name for tables (derived from source name)
required_settings.sslMode: SSL mode: disable, require, or verify-ca

optional_settings.sshHost: SSH tunnel host for tunneled connections

runtime_config.Warehouse.postgres.skipDedupDestinationI: Destination IDs to skip dedup for
runtime_config.Warehouse.postgres.skipComputingUserLate: Skip users table trait recomputation (default: false)
Workspace IDs to skip trait recomputation for

notes: PostgreSQL is a shared warehouse destination present in both RudderStack and Segment. Key architectural differences: (1) Segment uses direct SQL INSERT or COPY to load data; RudderStack uses file-download loading with gzipped CSV staging, pq.CopyIn for bulk streaming, and ROW_NUMBER() dedup. (2) RudderStack uniquely supports SSH tunneling for secure connections through bastion hosts. (3) RudderStack uses text/numeric/timestamptz types while Segment uses VARCHAR(512)/FLOAT/TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE — functionally equivalent. (4) RudderStack adds extra metadata columns (uuid_ts, context_passed_ip, context_request_ip, context_traits_*). (5) Users table computation differs: Segment uses incremental upserts, RudderStack uses batch CASE-based newest-value aggregation. Overall data parity is high (~85%) with differences limited to column types, additional metadata columns, and SDK library identifiers. Reference: warehouse/integrations/postgres/ package in rudder-server, docs/gap-report/destination-catalog-parity.md warehouse comparison table.
